newsitem.title: UK: Budget should see tight fiscal policy - forecasters.
newsitem.headline: Budget should see tight fiscal policy - forecasters.

text.p: Most of the British Treasury's six member panel of independent forecasters think the November budget should feature tighter fiscal policy, the panel said in a report on Friday.

"Three recommend a modest tightening of fiscal policy in response to the worsening prospect for the PSBR, and two would like to see government borrowing reduced by up to 1.0 percent of GDP," the half-yearly report said.
The panel made the following average forecasts --
"Demand has grown strongly so far this year, but stock adjustment has held back output growth, particularly in the manufacturing sector," the report said.
"Most of us think that the stock adjustment is now largely complete and we expect output to strengthen from now on, with GDP growing by 3.0 percent or more in 1997."

"Most of us expect inflation to be at or below the government"s 2.5 percent target at the end of next year, although five of us believe that strong demand growth will put upward pressure on inflation during 1998."
One of the six panel members saw scope for "significant tax cuts" in the budget.
Report based on information up to October 28 and before recent decision to raise UK base lending rates to 6.0 percent.
In the report, three forecasters said there was no need for a move in rates but they had a clear bias to future tightening.
Two felt rates should be raised and one argued for a cut.
